analysis.investment_thesis: Small-cap IT services at P/E 8.9x with net cash (post-IPO equity jumped ₹67cr→₹171cr in FY25) offers some margin of safety, but revenue growth has collapsed from a 28% 5Y CAGR to just 2% YoY in FY25 and operating income actually contracted (₹34cr→₹30cr). Cheap optics mask a potentially broken growth story in a commoditized niche — fair value, not a bargain.
key_strengths: Clean balance sheet: zero debt; IPO proceeds deployed (investing CF -₹77cr in FY25)
Strong returns on capital: ROE 20%, ROCE 26.5%; 5/5 years positive OCF
Undemanding P/E 8.9x with 74.67% promoter holding providing alignment
key_risks: Growth has stalled: revenue +2% YoY, EBITDA -9%, OCF -14% in FY25 — deceleration is real
Commoditized small-cap IT services; no visible moat vs global captive/offshoring giants
Recent IPO at cycle peak; float small (25%), liquidity and valuation de-rating risk
red_flags: FY25 operating income declined despite IPO cash infusion — margins compressing
₹6cr 'other income' boosting FY25 net profit; underlying operating profitability weakened
Investing CF -₹77cr suggests large treasury/non-core deployment rather than reinvestment in the business
analysis.detailed_analysis: Second-level thinking here: the market sees a ₹203cr IT micro-cap at 8.9x earnings with ~40% of market cap in net cash and asks "why so cheap?" The answer is in the FY25 print — revenue growth has essentially stopped (₹98cr→₹100cr), EBITDA contracted from ₹35cr to ₹32cr, and net profit only held flat because of a ₹6cr spike in other income (likely IPO-cash treasury yield). Strip that out and FY25 operating earnings are materially worse than FY24. That is the cycle-peak tell: the company IPO'd after a multi-year tailwind (global digital services boom post-2020) and the tailwind has turned.\n\nThat said, downside is contained. Book value is ~₹171cr against ₹203cr market cap, so you're paying ~₹32cr for a cash-generating business earning ₹26cr — a ~5x EV/earnings once you net cash. Promoter at 74.67% won't dump. If growth re-accelerates even to 10-12%, re-rating is plausible; if it doesn't, you're unlikely to lose much capital but your money dead-weights. Classic fair-risk/fair-reward — no margin-of-safety scream, no compelling asymmetry. Pass unless bought materially cheaper, or wait a quarter or two to see if FY26 revenue inflects before committing.
